original_question: Let f : {-1,1}^n -> {-1,1} be unbiased. For a random restriction z in {-1,0,1}^n where each coordinate is independently +1 or -1 with probability p/2 each and 0 with probability 1-p, with p < 1/2 and n odd, is E_z[|f(z)|] maximized when f is the majority function, identifying f with its multilinear expansion?
target_in_paper: The unnumbered statement titled "Non-Interactive Correlation Distillation with Erasures" in the main list of open problems.
correct_elements: Your draft already captures the exact target problem very closely: it has the right class of functions f:{-1,1}^n->{-1,1}, the unbiasedness assumption, the correct product distribution on z in {-1,0,1}^n, the regime p<1/2 with n odd, the objective E_z[|f(z)|], and the paper's crucial parenthetical that f is evaluated on z by identifying it with its multilinear expansion. ([arxiv.org](https://arxiv.org/pdf/1204.6447.pdf))
missing_details: Make the quantifiers explicit: the question is intended for every odd integer n and every admissible parameter p with p<1/2.
Define "unbiased" explicitly as E_{x uniform on {-1,1}^n}[f(x)]=0.
Specify that the comparator is the n-variable majority function Maj_n, not an unspecified majority on some other number of inputs.
Define majority explicitly, e.g. Maj_n(x)=sgn(x_1+...+x_n); the oddness of n guarantees no ties.
Spell out that f(z) means evaluation of the unique real multilinear polynomial agreeing with f on {-1,1}^n at the point z in {-1,0,1}^n.
State explicitly that the expectation is only over the random restriction z.
refined_question: For every odd integer n and every p with 0<=p<1/2, let f:{-1,1}^n->{-1,1} be unbiased, i.e. E_{x uniform on {-1,1}^n}[f(x)]=0. Let z=(z_1,...,z_n) in {-1,0,1}^n have independent coordinates with P(z_i=1)=P(z_i=-1)=p/2 and P(z_i=0)=1-p. Writing f^{ml} for the unique real multilinear polynomial that agrees with f on {-1,1}^n, is it always true that E_z[|f^{ml}(z)|] <= E_z[|Maj_n^{ml}(z)|], where Maj_n(x)=sgn(x_1+...+x_n) is the n-bit majority function?
justification: The draft is aiming at the paper's exact official problem statement, not a neighboring variant: the paper states this as "Non-Interactive Correlation Distillation with Erasures" and uses essentially the same wording. The only paper-faithful refinements needed to make it fully stand-alone are to unpack the standard meaning of "unbiased," make the universal quantifiers explicit, specify that the comparison is with Maj_n on the same odd number n of inputs, and define precisely what it means to evaluate f at z in {-1,0,1}^n via the multilinear expansion. The nearby remark bullets also show that the scope should stay exactly in the p<1/2 regime: for p>=1/2 the conjectured extremizer changes to dictator, while Mossel's result is only an approximate majority bound under a low-influence assumption. ([arxiv.org](https://arxiv.org/pdf/1204.6447.pdf))
